scenes.heading: Solving Equations
scenes.narration: Welcome to part three of our Grade 9 algebra series. In this lesson we solve equations with brackets, with fractions, and by factorising.

scenes.heading: Example 1: Brackets
scenes.narration: Solve four times, x minus two, minus three times, x plus one, equals five. Expand: four x minus eight, minus three x, minus three. Careful: negative three times positive one is negative three. Simplify the left side: x minus eleven equals five. Add eleven to both sides, and x equals sixteen.

scenes.heading: Example 2: Fractions
scenes.narration: Solve x over three, plus x over two, equals ten. The lowest common denominator is six, so multiply every term by six, including the ten. Six times x over three is two x. Six times x over two is three x. Six times ten is sixty. So five x equals sixty, and x equals twelve.

scenes.heading: Example 3: Fraction on each side
scenes.narration: Solve x plus one over four, equals x minus two over three. Multiply both sides by twelve, or cross multiply, to get three times x plus one, equals four times x minus two. Expand: three x plus three equals four x minus eight. Move the terms: three x minus four x equals negative eight minus three. So negative x equals negative eleven, and x equals eleven.

scenes.heading: When a product equals zero
bullets: Get zero on one side, factorise, then set each factor equal to zero
These equations can have two answers
scenes.narration: Here is a powerful idea. If two numbers multiply to give zero, then at least one of them must be zero. So to solve an equation with x squared, get zero on one side, factorise, and set each factor equal to zero. These equations can have two answers.

scenes.heading: Example 4
scenes.narration: Solve x squared minus five x equals zero. Take out the common factor x: x times, x minus five, equals zero. So x equals zero, or x minus five equals zero. The answers are x equals zero, or x equals five. Do not divide by x, or you will lose the answer zero.

scenes.heading: Example 5
scenes.narration: Solve x squared plus x minus twelve equals zero. We need two numbers that multiply to negative twelve and add to one: four and negative three. So x plus four, times x minus three, equals zero. Therefore x equals negative four, or x equals three.

scenes.heading: Tips
bullets: With fractions, multiply every term by the LCD
A minus in front of a bracket changes every sign inside
For $x^2$ equations: zero on one side, then factorise
scenes.narration: Three tips. With fractions, multiply every single term by the lowest common denominator. A minus sign in front of a bracket changes every sign inside it. And for equations with x squared, get zero on one side, then factorise.

activity.title: Solving equations
